text:
Alex: quick note from today's replay runs — seeing instability in kernel selection between runs causing p99 jitter (~9%).
Maya: is the replayer running with the same binary/config as prod?
Alex: yes. Same binary. Difference is anonymization: we drop request_id/session headers which zero out RNG entropy used for kernel tie-breaking. Replayer seed ends up effectively random each run.
Ken: we should add an explicit seed flag and deterministic tiebreak policy.
Sara: +1. Also noticed KV hit ratios are much lower in replay vs prod — anonymized session ids break cache affinity.
Alex: example log snippet from a problematic replay:
```
[replayer] start seed=0x00000000
[kernel-picker] candidates=[matmul_8x, matmul_16x] costs=[12.005,12.003] tiebreak=random pick=matmul_8x
[kv] miss key=session-0000
```
Maya: two possible fixes: (A) have anonymizer emit deterministic pseudo-ids derived from original request metadata (preserve mapping but anonymized), (B) add replayer flags: --seed, --kernel-tiebreak=stable, --preserve-headers, --preserve-interarrival.
Ken: for session affinity reconstruction i propose grouping proximate requests by hashed src_ip + time bucket so generated anon-session ids maintain local continuity and allow KV warmups. Call it "affine-session" mapping.
Sara: agree. Also we should stop normalizing timestamps to coarse buckets — that flattens bursts and changes batching. Preserve interarrival times for apples-to-apples batching.
Maya: quick anonymizer sketch:
```
ip_hash = sha256(src_ip + salt)
bucket = floor(ts / 30)  # 30s affinity window
anon_session = hex_slice(sha256(ip_hash + bucket), 8)
request_id = anon_session + '_' + seq
emit header X-Anon-Session: anon_session
```
Alex: don't forget to replay SDK hints too — we dropped batch_id header previously and runtime batching heuristics no longer saw the hint.
Ken: test plan suggestion:
- baseline: 50 replays with current anonymizer (randomized)
- experiment: 50 replays with deterministic seed + affine-session + preserved headers
- metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies, kernel pick distribution, kv_hit_rate, batching size dist, per-token timing histograms
- success criteria: kernel distribution delta < 1%, kv_hit_rate delta < 3%, tail latency within expected noise band
Sara: we should add a parity assertion harness in the replayer that compares outputs + timing histograms. If kernel differs but outputs and timing are within epsilon, pass; else mark as divergence.
Alex: should replayer be deterministic by default for prod-trace runs? I think yes. Keep random default for synthetic fuzzing.
Maya: agree. default mode: if input trace has metadata field "prod=true" -> deterministic. Otherwise RNG-enabled.
infra-bot: note: replayer v0.10.0 queued for staging with flags: --seed, --kernel-tiebreak=stable, --preserve-headers, --preserve-interarrival.
Ken: action items:
- Ken: add --seed and --kernel-tiebreak (PR today)
- Maya: implement affine-session + preserve SDK headers in anonymizer (tomorrow)
- Sara: implement parity assertion harness and include kv_hit + kernel-dist metrics in replay report (this week)
- infra-bot: schedule staging runs and upload artifacts here
infra-bot: staging replays scheduled 2024-03-05T02:00Z: 50 baseline, 50 deterministic. Artifacts: /artifacts/replays/1725508000/
Maya: i'll attach a minimal example anonymized trace so infra can reproduce locally.
Alex: once we get kernel-pick and KV affinity parity, replays can be used reliably for perf regression gating. Will follow up with results.
Sara: also add a short checklist to replayer README: exact flags, dataset tags, success criteria — makes future apples-to-apples runs reproducible.
Ken: will add README section and a small script wrapper that runs baseline+experiment and outputs a diff report.
Alex: thanks all, closing here. Post results/artifacts and i'll review before we flip any CI gates.
